name: Serenity
tagline: Proof-of-concept Redis-compatible server with ACID transactions on the Sophia disk engine; abandoned in 2016.
description: Serenity was a 2015-2016 experiment by Dmitry Simonenko, author of the Sophia storage engine, to put a Redis-compatible front end on disk-based storage. It implemented the basic Redis commands and configuration format so redis-cli, redis-benchmark, memtier and existing Redis drivers worked unchanged, but stored data in Sophia's append-only MVCC engine so datasets could be much larger than RAM, and added consistent cursors, real ACID transactions and stored procedures. The README always called it a proof of concept, and development stopped in July 2016. Disk-backed Redis-protocol servers such as Kvrocks and Pika now fill this role.
statusNote: Proof of concept with no commits since July 2016. For a disk-backed Redis-compatible store use Apache Kvrocks or Pika.

scale.notes: Single server; data could exceed RAM thanks to the Sophia disk engine.

strengths: Drop-in Redis protocol and config compatibility with existing tools
Datasets larger than memory via the Sophia MVCC engine
Real ACID transactions and consistent cursors beyond what Redis offered
weaknesses: Explicitly a proof of concept; only basic Redis commands
The underlying Sophia engine has had no code changes since 2019
useCases: Studying how to layer the Redis protocol over a disk engine
Historical comparison with Kvrocks, Pika and other disk-backed Redis servers
notIdealFor: Workloads needing the full Redis command set
